videos.title: If You Feel Guilty About Stepping Back From Family, Please Watch This | Dr. Ramani
videos.description:
People think you cut off family over one bad moment. It's never one moment. It's the last of 1,500 others.

In this clip, Dr. Ramani Durvasula and Jay Shetty talk about how you know it's time to cut off a toxic family member. Dr. Ramani explains the "natural experiment." It can show you the truth about a relationship without you saying a word.

She opens up about her own no contact decision, one that took 40 years to make. She shares why the people who walk away are often the ones who tried hardest to fix things. And she explains what to say when the whole family starts pushing back.

Learn the one sign that shows someone can really change. And learn why forgiveness isn't always the healthy choice.

videos.title: Claude Code + Obsidian: My family’s AI brain
videos.description:
Scott Farrar is a math educator and parent who got tired of AI chats that drift and forget. So he built a household brain in Claude Code: a folder of Markdown files, viewed in Obsidian, that knows his appliances, warranties, insurance documents, and everything on his family’s to-do list. In this episode, Scott shows how he uses it to shop for car insurance, plan repairs, share the system with his wife, and put priority tasks and recent wins on a wall display. We also talk about AI and math learning, and why he wants AI to keep kids doing the thinking.

*What you’ll learn:*
1. Why he moved his home life from AI chat to Claude Code
2. What Claude told him to photograph first
3. How AI made him a sharper insurance shopper
4. The to-do file he keeps coming back to
5. How he and his wife share one household brain
6. Why his wall display has a “recent wins” section
7. How a flipped tutor gets kids to teach the AI

videos.title: I was a Claude hater. Fable 5.2 changed my mind.
videos.description:
Anthropic just released Fable 5.2, their new frontier model, and I spent two days actually building things with it before recording this. I made an animated marketing video from a single tweet, assembled a pile of unboxed furniture using only blurry floor photos, and extended our CXO brand sprites into a full bug-defense game complete with a trailer. In this episode I walk through what impressed me, what fell short, and how I’m thinking about routing tasks between Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 going forward.

*What you'll learn:*
1. What Anthropic launched with Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, and when to reach for Fable instead of Opus 5.5
2. My pros and cons after a couple of days of hands-on testing
3. How Fable 5.2 turned a tweet and a brand book into an animated video that doesn’t look like slides
4. The geometry test every other model failed: assembly instructions for flat-pack furniture with no manual
5. How it handled a real re-architecture of ChatPRD’s product intelligence pipeline
6. Why I still wouldn’t let it design a website on its own
7. The 3D typewriter it built me, and how you can get access to the model

*In this episode, we cover:*
(00:00) Confessions of a Claude hater
(02:54) What Anthropic launched: Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2

If you’re thinking, “I would never manipulate anyone,” I have some bad news. Ever praised a dinner you didn’t love, or flattered someone right before asking for a favor? So where’s the line? Drew and I start with a philosopher who said you shouldn’t lie even to a murderer at your door, and the simple test he landed on years later that still holds up.
